 LAS VEGAS (KSNV) — A Las Vegas tax preparer who prosecutors say helped file false federal returns seeking more than $5 million in improper refunds has been sentenced to more than three years in prison.
 Ivan Odiaga was sentenced Wednesday to 38 months in prison for conspiring to defraud the United States by filing false tax returns with the IRS and diverting portions of the resulting tax refunds to himself and his co-defendant.
 According to court documents and statements made in court, Odiaga prepared federal income tax returns at Silver State Tax & Multiservices LLC, a Las Vegas tax preparation business owned by his mother and co-defendant, Iris Hondermann. From approximately 2017 through 2021, Odiaga and Hondermann prepared tax returns for clients that included one or more false items, including business profits and losses, COVID-19 sick and family leave credits, and residential energy credits.
 In 2020 and 2021, Odiaga prepared some returns using another tax preparer's Preparer Tax Identification Number without permission, according to court documents and statements made in court.

 Between 2017 and 2021, Odiaga and Hondermann prepared false tax returns filed with the IRS seeking more than $5 million in refunds that their clients were not entitled to receive, authorities said. Prosecutors said the pair at times also diverted portions of client tax refunds to themselves, and that from 2017 through 2021 they diverted more than $1.1 million in fraudulent tax refunds to bank accounts one or both of them controlled.
 Hondermann previously pleaded guilty on Aug. 5 to one count of conspiring to defraud the United States.
